name: Question 8
problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of the acceleration is $k{x}^{3}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant, and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$ If $P$ has velocity $v=8\sqrt{17}\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has a velocity of $v=8\,m/s$ when its displacement is $4\,m,$ find the value of $k.$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14164351/assets/f3879ccc6084d9a0ef8bef2e211e2e7fd9dcc811fb04f06c2ef7429e4d574871.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ has magnitude $k{x}^{3}\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-k{x}^{3}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-k{x}^{3}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (-k{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=8\sqrt{17}\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{17})^{2} & =-\frac{k}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =544\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=544-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=4\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =544-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4} \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =544-\frac{k}{4}(4)^{4} \\ 32 & =544-64k \\ 64k & =512 \\ k & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Since the acceleration of the particle P has magnitude kx3m/s2 and is directed toward O, we have

dvdt=−kx3.

Using the fact that dvdt=ddx(12v2), we can rewrite our equation as

ddx(12v2)=−kx3.

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to x, we have

∫ddx(12v2)dx=∫(−kx3)dx

which gives the general solution

12v2=−k4x4+C.

Now, since v=817m/s when x=0m, we can find the value of the constant C, as follows:

12v2=−k4x4+C12(817)2=−k4(0)4+CC=544

Therefore,

12v2=544−k4x4.

Finally, since v=8m/s when x=4m, we can find the value of the positive constant k, as follows:

12v2=544−k4x412(8)2=544−k4(4)432=544−64k64k=512k=8.
